definition_zh: 毁林；森林砍伐；森林覆盖的丧失
definition_en: the removal or clearing of forest cover, usually to convert the land to another use
core_image: 推土机沿山坡推进，成片的树倒下后被烧掉，裸露的红土被雨水冲成沟壑
scene: 推土机沿山坡推进，成片的树倒下后被烧掉，裸露的红土在雨季被冲成沟壑。 Bulldozers moved along the slope, felled trees were burned in heaps, and the bare red soil was cut into gullies by the rains: this is deforestation.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「把森林清除掉的过程」（第 1 个义项：森林被砍伐清除）；句意为推土机沿坡推进，伐倒的树被烧掉，裸露红土被雨水冲出沟壑，这就是毁林。

pos.zh: 被清除后的状态或结果
作为环境驱动因素的毁林
历史上为农业而进行的林地清除

senses.title: Clearing forest
senses.definition: the act of cutting or burning forest to remove tree cover
senses.definitionCN: 通过砍伐或焚烧除去森林覆盖的行为
senses.example: Deforestation begins with roads cut into the forest edge.
senses.exampleCN: 毁林从在森林边缘开出道路开始。
senses.why: This is the core act sense: the trees are deliberately removed.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心行为义：树木被有意清除。

senses.title: Loss of forest cover
senses.definition: the process by which a forested area loses its tree cover over time
senses.definitionCN: 林地在时间中失去树木覆盖的过程
senses.example: Satellite images showed deforestation spreading along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星图像显示毁林沿河流蔓延。
senses.why: The act is now viewed as a process measured in area and time.
senses.whyCN: 行为此时被看作以面积和时间衡量的过程。

senses.title: Conversion to other land use
senses.definition: the change of forest land into farmland, pasture, settlement or infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 把林地改为农田、牧场、居民点或基础设施
senses.example: Much deforestation here is conversion to cattle pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的毁林大多是改为养牛牧场。
senses.why: The word names the loss from the forest's side, while land-use writing names the gain from the new use's side.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从森林一侧命名损失，而土地利用写作从新用途一侧命名获得。

senses.title: Large-scale logging
senses.definition: the removal of timber over large areas, often for export or industry
senses.definitionCN: 在大面积上采伐木材，常为出口或工业原料
senses.example: Selective logging is not the same as deforestation.
senses.exampleCN: 选择性采伐与毁林不是一回事。
senses.why: Logging removes trees; deforestation means the forest cover does not return.
senses.whyCN: 采伐移走树木；毁林意味着森林覆盖不再恢复。

senses.title: Cleared state
senses.definition: the condition of land after its forest has been removed
senses.definitionCN: 森林被除去后土地所处的状态
senses.example: The deforested slope lost its soil within two seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 被毁林的山坡在两个季节内就失去了土壤。
senses.why: The action noun also names the resulting landscape, which is what later restoration must address.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词也命名结果景观，而这正是后来恢复要面对的对象。

senses.title: Tropical deforestation
senses.definition: the clearing of tropical forests, especially for agriculture and ranching
senses.definitionCN: 热带森林的清除，尤因农业与牧业
senses.example: Tropical deforestation accounts for a large share of emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 热带毁林占排放的很大一部分。
senses.why: The general word is attached to its most politically visible setting.
senses.whyCN: 这个总称词被固定在其最受关注的具体场景上。

senses.title: Environmental driver
senses.definition: deforestation considered as a cause of biodiversity loss, erosion and carbon emissions
senses.definitionCN: 把毁林看作生物多样性丧失、侵蚀与碳排放的原因
senses.example: The report links deforestation to both flooding and species decline.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把毁林与洪水及物种减少都联系起来。
senses.why: The word shifts from an event to a causal factor in environmental systems.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从事件转成环境系统中的因果因素。

senses.title: Historical clearance
senses.definition: the clearing of forest in earlier periods, often for farming or fuel
senses.definitionCN: 较早时期为农业或燃料而清除森林
senses.example: Medieval deforestation left only small woods on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的毁林只在山脊上留下小片树林。
senses.why: The modern word is applied retrospectively to older land-use change.
senses.whyCN: 现代词被追溯用于更早的土地用途改变。

intro.en: Deforestation is a nineteenth-century formation on de- plus forestation. Its rise as a global environmental term belongs to the twentieth century, and the first date is approximate.
intro.cn: 该词为十九世纪由 de- 加 forestation 构成；成为全球环境术语主要在二十世纪，确切首见年代为大致估计。

items.en: The prefix de- means 'away, down, reversing'. Forest comes from Medieval Latin forestis through Old French, and -ation from Latin -atio marks an action or result.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 意为「离开、向下、反转」。forest 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 forestis，-ation 来自拉丁语 -atio，标记动作或结果。

items.en: Deforestation is recorded in nineteenth-century writing on land use, often in descriptions of clearing for farms or fuel. French déforestation may have reinforced the form.
items.cn: deforestation 见于十九世纪有关土地利用的写作，常描述为农田或燃料而进行的清除。法语 déforestation 可能强化了这一形式。

items.en: The term became global with tropical forest loss after the mid-twentieth century, when satellites made the loss visible as area and rate.
items.cn: 二十世纪中期以后，随着热带森林丧失，这个词走向全球；卫星让损失以面积与速度变得可见。

items.en: Climate and biodiversity policy made deforestation a driver to be measured, reported and regulated, including through zero-deforestation supply chains.
items.cn: 气候与生物多样性政策把毁林变成需要测量、报告与监管的驱动因素，包括零毁林供应链。

items.en: The word now covers deliberate clearing, agricultural conversion and the resulting loss of cover, and is often used retrospectively for earlier centuries.
items.cn: 这个词现在涵盖有意清除、农业转换以及由此造成的覆盖丧失，也常被追溯用于更早的世纪。

note.en: The first group is close in form but names a different act or a different scale; the second group shares the removal or loss meaning without being interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组在形式上接近，但命名不同行为或不同尺度；第二组共享清除或丧失的意思，但不能互换。

entries.definition: the establishment of forest cover; it is the reverse of deforestation, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 造林。建立森林覆盖，是毁林的相反过程，不是同义词。

entries.definition: planting forest on land without recent forest; it is a kind of forestation, not a kind of deforestation.
entries.definitionCN: 新造林。在近期无林地上造林，是造林的一种，不是毁林的一种。

entries.definition: a change of shape, from forma 'form'; it has no forest element.
entries.definitionCN: 变形。来自 forma「形状」，不含森林成分。

entries.definition: the general removal of trees or obstacles from land; it can be small-scale and need not mean permanent forest loss.
entries.definitionCN: 清除；清理。从土地上移除树木或障碍，可小规模，也不必然意味着永久失去森林。

entries.definition: the cutting and transporting of timber; it may leave the forest able to regenerate, unlike deforestation.
entries.definitionCN: 伐木。砍伐与运输木材，森林可能仍能更新，不像毁林那样。

entries.definition: the removal of vegetation to prepare land for another use; it is the purpose-neutral description of the same act.
entries.definitionCN: 土地清理。为准备其他用途而清除植被，是对同一行为的用途中立描述。

entries.definition: the net loss of forest area or quality; it includes degradation as well as complete clearing.
entries.definitionCN: 森林丧失。森林面积或质量的净损失，包括退化与完全清除。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is de- 'away' plus forestation, so it literally means the undoing of forest creation.
normal.cn: 这个词是 de-「去除」加 forestation，字面就是「取消造林的结果」。

normal.en: The family runs deforest, deforested, deforestation-free and reforestation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 deforest、deforested、deforestation-free 与 reforestation。

normal.en: Collocations: tropical deforestation, deforestation rate, deforestation driver.
normal.cn: 搭配：热带毁林、毁林速度、毁林驱动因素。

normal.en: Logging removes trees, but deforestation means the cover does not return.
normal.cn: 伐木移走树木，但毁林意味着覆盖不再恢复。

normal.en: Zero-deforestation supply chains are a policy instrument of the 2010s.
normal.cn: 零毁林供应链是二十一世纪一十年代的政策工具。

abstract.en: Picture a road pushed into intact forest, with bare ground widening behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路推进完整森林，后面裸地不断变宽。

abstract.en: Picture a satellite image where a green block turns brown year by year.
abstract.cn: 想象卫星图上一块绿色逐年变褐。

abstract.en: Picture smoke from burned felled trees rising over a hillside of stumps.
abstract.cn: 想象被烧的伐倒木冒烟，下方是布满树桩的山坡。

examples.en: Deforestation in the basin reduced dry-season water storage.
examples.cn: 流域内的毁林减少了旱季的蓄水量。

examples.en: The company pledged to remove deforestation from its supply chain.
examples.cn: 该公司承诺从供应链中消除毁林。

examples.en: Historical deforestation left the ridge with thin, eroded soils.
examples.cn: 历史上的林地清除让山脊只剩薄而受侵蚀的土壤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「去掉 + 森林」——把森林覆盖从土地上拿掉 → 毁林

root: 由 de-「去除」加 forestation 构成，十九世纪见于土地利用写作；forest 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 forestis。作为全球环境术语主要在二十世纪流行，确切首见年代为大致估计。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the act of clearing to the process of loss, the land-use conversion, the logging that may or may not cause it, the resulting landscape, the tropical setting, the environmental causal role and retrospective historical clearance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从清除行为，到丧失过程、土地用途转换、可能造成也可能不造成毁林的采伐、结果景观、热带场景、环境因果角色，再到追溯性的历史林地清除。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green block being cut back to bare soil, year after year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块绿色被逐年削回裸土。

branches.en: ACT AND PROCESS: deliberate clearing and the measured loss it produces.
branches.cn: 行为与过程：有意清除，以及它造成的可测丧失。

branches.en: CONVERSION AND LOGGING: one changes the use, the other removes timber; only the first is necessarily deforestation.
branches.cn: 转换与采伐：前者改变用途，后者移走木材；只有前者必然是毁林。

branches.en: THE BARE RESULT: land left without its cover.
branches.cn: 裸露的结果：失去覆盖后的土地。

branches.en: TROPICS AND DRIVERS: the most visible setting and the causal role in climate and biodiversity.
branches.cn: 热带与驱动：最显眼的场景，以及在气候与生物多样性中的因果角色。

branches.en: RETROSPECT: the modern word applied to old land-use change.
branches.cn: 回溯：现代词用于旧的土地用途改变。

intro.en: Deforestation is a transparent English formation whose parts come from Latin and French; the affix section separates the reversing prefix from the forest base and the action suffix.
intro.cn: deforestation 是透明的英语构造，各成分来自拉丁语与法语；词缀部分把反转前缀与森林基础词、动作后缀分开。

latinIntro.en: Latin de- supplies the reversing prefix, Medieval Latin forestis supplies the base, and Latin -atio supplies the action suffix. The French form may have reinforced the English one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 de- 提供反转前缀，中世纪拉丁语 forestis 提供基础，拉丁语 -atio 提供动作后缀。法语形式可能强化了英语形式。

items.exampleCN: 该公司因清除保护区森林被罚款。

items.meaning: net loss of forest area or quality

items.exampleCN: 土地清理是用途中立的描述。

definition_zh: 使变形；压坏形状；使扭曲；使失真；使成畸形
definition_en: to change or spoil the shape of something, or to make a material, image or body part lose its proper form
core_image: 夹具夹得太紧，薄壁圆管被压扁了一点，圆度计读出偏差
scene: 夹具夹得太紧，薄壁圆管被压扁了一点，圆度计读出偏差。Too much clamping pressure can deform the thin tube.
sceneCN: 这里指外力把物体原来的形状压坏（第 1 个义项：使形状改变）；句意为过大的夹紧力会使薄壁管变形。图中可辨识物件：薄壁管、夹具、圆度计、压力表、扁痕。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「形变；变形」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「变形的；畸形的」
由该动词加表示「可……的」的形容词尾构成，义为「可变形的」
由同一词干加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「畸形」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「使变形的工具或人」

senses.title: To change a shape by force
senses.definition: to change the shape or dimensions of an object by applying force, heat or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 通过施加力、热或压力来改变物体的形状或尺寸
senses.example: The clamp can deform the pipe if it is overtightened.
senses.exampleCN: 夹具拧得太紧会使管子变形。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to put out of shape, and the physical act remains the base of every other sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「使失去形状」，这个物理动作是其余各义的基础。

senses.title: To bend out of true
senses.definition: to bend or sag so that a body no longer has its intended shape
senses.definitionCN: 弯曲或下垂，使物体不再具有原本设定的形状
senses.example: The shelf began to deform under the weight.
senses.exampleCN: 搁板在重压下开始变形。
senses.why: An object can deform without an obvious hand on it, and the verb covers that slow sag.
senses.whyCN: 物件可以在没有明显外力的情况下变形，这个动词覆盖那种缓慢的下垂。

senses.title: To shape metal by force
senses.definition: to change the shape of a material deliberately as part of a forming process
senses.definitionCN: 作为成形工艺的一部分，有意改变材料的形状
senses.example: The press deforms the sheet into a shallow bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 压机把板料压成浅碗形。
senses.why: In metal work, deformation is not damage but the intended operation, and the verb is neutral.
senses.whyCN: 在金属加工里，变形不是损坏而是预期操作，这个动词是中性词。

senses.title: To distort a form
senses.definition: to spoil the natural or intended outline of something so that it looks wrong
senses.definitionCN: 破坏某物自然或预期的轮廓，使其看起来不对劲
senses.example: Heat deformed the plastic housing.
senses.exampleCN: 受热使塑料外壳走了形。
senses.why: The eye judges outline, and anything bent out of its true line reads as deformed.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛判断轮廓，任何弯离正确线条的东西都显得变形。

senses.title: To make a body part malformed
senses.definition: to cause a part of a living body to grow or set in an abnormal shape
senses.definitionCN: 使活体的某一部分长成或固定成异常形状
senses.example: The injury deformed the joint over time.
senses.exampleCN: 那次损伤随时间使关节变形。
senses.why: Medicine uses the verb for shape that has gone wrong in tissue, whether from growth or trauma.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个动词指组织中出了错的形状，无论源于生长还是创伤。

senses.title: To distort an image or signal
senses.definition: to alter an image, waveform or dataset so that it no longer represents the original faithfully
senses.definitionCN: 改变图像、波形或数据集，使其不再忠实反映原物
senses.example: A cheap lens deforms the edges of the picture.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价镜头会使画面边缘失真。
senses.why: A picture has a shape, and a lens that bends it is said to deform it.
senses.whyCN: 画面有形状，把它弄弯的镜头就被说成使它变形。

senses.title: To bend the ground
senses.definition: to cause rock or soil to fold, subside or shift under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下使岩石或土壤褶皱、沉降或位移
senses.example: The excavation deformed the slope above the road.
senses.exampleCN: 开挖使公路上方的坡体变形。
senses.why: The ground behaves as a solid under long pressure, and geology uses the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 地层在长期压力下像固体一样行为，地质学用同一个动词。

senses.title: To twist the truth
senses.definition: to distort a statement, record or meaning so that it misrepresents what happened
senses.definitionCN: 歪曲陈述、记录或含义，使其错误地呈现事实
senses.example: The summary deforms what the report actually says.
senses.exampleCN: 这份摘要歪曲了报告的实际内容。
senses.why: Meaning is given a shape, and bending it away from the truth is the same metaphor as bending metal.
senses.whyCN: 意义被赋予形状，把它弯离事实与弯金属是同一个比喻。

intro.en: Deform comes from Latin deformare, to put out of shape, from de, away from, and forma, shape. English took the verb through French, and the technical senses grew out of the plain one.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 deformare「使失去形状」，由 de「离开」与 forma「形状」构成。英语经法语引入这个动词，技术义从朴素义发展而来。

items.en: Forma meant shape, form or mould, and it is the element that keeps the word about visible figure.
items.cn: 这个词意为形状、形式或模具，是使这个词始终关乎可见外形的成分。

items.en: The prefix meant away from or down, and it marks the loss of the proper shape rather than a new one.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「离开、向下」，标出的是失去原有形状，而不是获得新形状。

items.en: The verb meant to shape badly, disfigure or mar, and it applied to faces, bodies and objects.
items.cn: 这个动词意为弄坏形状、毁容、损毁，可用于面孔、身体与物件。

items.en: Old French deformar carried the verb into English, where it first described spoiled outward form.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入英语，最初描述被破坏的外形。

items.en: Industrial forming made the verb neutral, naming the intended change of shape; the first attestation date is uncertain.
items.cn: 工业成形使这个动词变成中性，指有意的形状改变；首见年代不确定。

items.en: The twentieth century extended the verb to lenses and signals, and older uses kept it for the body and for truth.
items.cn: 二十世纪把这个动词扩展到镜头与信号，较早的用法则把它留在身体与真相上。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like deform; the second group names neighbouring ideas of bending and spoiling shape.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「deform」相近；第二组是与「弯曲、弄坏形状」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the change of shape or the resulting distorted form.
entries.definitionCN: 指形状改变或由此产生的扭曲形态。

entries.definition: The adjective for something whose shape has been spoiled.
entries.definitionCN: 指形状已被弄坏的形容词。

entries.definition: A bodily malformation, usually structural rather than caused by a single load.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体畸形，通常是结构性的，而非单次载荷造成。

entries.definition: To improve or reshape something; it uses the shape word with a prefix meaning again.
entries.definitionCN: 指改良或重塑某物；用同一个「形状」词干，前缀意为「再次」。

entries.definition: To damage someone's reputation; it looks close but comes from the word for fame.
entries.definitionCN: 指损害他人名誉；形近，但来自表示「名声」的词。

entries.definition: To twist something out of its true shape or meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物扭离真实形状或含义。

entries.definition: To make something curved rather than straight.
To twist out of shape, especially through heat or moisture.
entries.definitionCN: 指扭曲变形，尤因受热或受潮。

entries.definition: To bend suddenly under compression, as a thin plate or rail does.
entries.definitionCN: 指受压突然弯曲，如薄板或钢轨。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real away-from-shape source, the real family and real shop phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「离开形状」来源、真实同族词与真实车间说法。

normal.en: Deform is de plus form: take the form away.
normal.cn: deform 就是「去掉」加「形状」：把形状拿走。

normal.en: Deformation is the noun, deformed the adjective, deformity the bodily form.
normal.cn: 形变是名词，变形的 是形容词，畸形是身体形态。

normal.en: Deform under load is the phrase on every material test.
normal.cn: 在载荷下变形是每种材料试验上的说法。

normal.en: A press deforms the sheet on purpose; a clamp deforms the pipe by mistake.
normal.cn: 压机有意使板料变形，夹具却误使管子变形。

normal.en: Reform uses the same shape stem with a prefix meaning again.
normal.cn: reform 用同一个「形状」词干，只是前缀意为「再次」。

abstract.en: To deform is to leave a mark that the object did not choose.
abstract.cn: 使变形就是在物体上留下一个它没有选择的痕迹。

abstract.en: The same verb bends steel and bends a sentence.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既弯钢，也弯句子。

abstract.en: A deformed truth is still the truth with its shape taken away.
abstract.cn: 被歪曲的事实，仍然是被拿走了形状的事实。

examples.en: Do not deform the seal when you fit the cover.
examples.cn: 装端盖时不要使密封件变形。

examples.en: The impact deformed the guard but saved the frame.
examples.cn: 撞击使护板变形，却保住了框架。

examples.en: A bad lens will deform the whole image.
examples.cn: 劣质镜头会使整幅图像失真。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪福姆」——把形状「迪」地改掉、不再有原来的形：使变形

root: 拉丁语 deformare「使失去形状」← de-「离开」+ forma「形状」，经法语进入英语。原义为毁坏外形，工业成形使它变成中性词，二十世纪又扩展到镜头与信号；各义定型的确切年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all take a shape away: by force, by sagging, by deliberate forming, by heat, by injury, by a lens, by excavation, and by a misleading summary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在拿走一个形状：用外力、靠下垂、有意成形、受热、受伤、镜头、开挖与误导性的摘要。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clamp closes on a thin tube and the round section turns oval.
core.cn: 核心意象：夹具夹住薄壁管，圆截面变成椭圆。

branches.en: THE LOADED BODY: a pipe squeezed by a clamp and a shelf sagging slowly.
branches.cn: 受力之物：被夹具挤住的管子，以及慢慢下垂的搁板。

branches.en: THE INTENDED FORMING: a press turning sheet into a bowl on purpose.
branches.cn: 有意的成形：压机有意把板料压成碗。

branches.en: THE SPOILED FORM: a housing warped by heat and a joint changed by injury.
branches.cn: 被弄坏的形状：受热走样的外壳，以及受伤改变的关节。

branches.en: THE DISTORTED WORLD: a lens bending edges, and a slope moving after excavation.
branches.cn: 被扭曲的世界：镜头把边缘弄弯，以及开挖后移动的坡体。

branches.en: THE BENT MEANING: a summary that takes the shape of the truth away.
branches.cn: 被弯的意义：把事实形状拿走的摘要。

intro.en: Deform is a Latin verb built on the word for shape, and its English family covers damage, medicine and images.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在「形状」一词上的拉丁动词，其英语词族覆盖损坏、医学与影像。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma and the prefix de- are the real parts; the verb deformare is attested and is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 forma 与前缀 de- 是真实构件；动词 deformare 有文献，是直接来源。

items.example: The noun is the shape being lost.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词就是被失去的形状。

items.example: The verb is attested in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在拉丁语文献中有据。

items.example: The positive verb shows the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 肯定动词显示同一个词干。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「形变」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「变形的」
由该动词加表示「可……的」的形容词尾构成，义为「可变形的」
由同一词干加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「畸形」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「使变形的工具」

definition_zh: adj. 已死的；不再存在的；已废止的；不再运作的
definition_en: no longer existing, functioning or in use
core_image: 一家老工厂大门挂着锁，招牌上的字被雨冲淡，里面再没有人上班
scene: 那条铁路早已停用。The railway is now defunct.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：defunct 指不再运作；句意是那条铁路现在已经停用。

pos.zh: 已死的；不再存在的；已废止的；不再运作的

senses.title: No longer alive
senses.definition: dead; no longer living
senses.definitionCN: 死了的；不再活着的
senses.example: The defunct king lay in state.
senses.exampleCN: 已故的国王停灵供人瞻仰。
senses.why: A body whose work has stopped.
senses.whyCN: 一具工作已经停下的身体。

senses.title: No longer operating
senses.definition: no longer functioning or in use
senses.definitionCN: 不再运转或不再使用
senses.example: The railway is now defunct.
senses.exampleCN: 那条铁路现在已经停用。
senses.why: A locked gate and an empty shift board.
senses.whyCN: 一把锁住的门和一块空白的排班板。

senses.title: No longer in force
senses.definition: no longer legally valid or effective
senses.definitionCN: 不再具有法律效力
senses.example: The defunct rule was struck from the book.
senses.exampleCN: 那条已废止的规则从册子里删掉了。
senses.why: A stamp cancelled with a line through it.
senses.whyCN: 一枚被划了一道线的作废印章。

intro.en: Defunct comes from Latin defunctus, having finished, from de- plus fungi, to perform.
intro.cn: defunct 源自拉丁语 defunctus（已完成），由 de- 加 fungi（履行、执行）构成。

items.en: Fungi meant to perform or discharge a duty.
items.cn: fungi 意为履行或完成职责。

items.en: Defungi meant to finish a duty completely.
items.cn: defungi 意为彻底完成职责。

items.en: Defunctus meant having finished, and so dead.
items.cn: defunctus 意为已完成，因而指已死。

items.en: Defunct entered English for the dead.
items.cn: 十五世纪 defunct 以已死义进入英语。

items.en: Defunct widened to things no longer in use.
items.cn: 十八世纪 defunct 扩展到不再使用的事物。

items.en: Defunct became common for closed organisations.
items.cn: 二十世纪 defunct 常用于已关闭的机构。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the funct- doing family; the near-meaning group names what has ended.
note.cn: 形近组共享 funct-（履行）家族；近义组都是「已经结束」的说法。

entries.definition: The special role or purpose of something.
Failure to work normally.
To remove the fuse from a bomb, or calm a situation.
No longer existing as a species.
No longer used because something newer exists.
Officially put an end to.
Not active now but able to become active.

normalIntro.en: Defunct is de- plus fungi, to perform: the duty is finished, so the thing is done.
normalIntro.cn: defunct 就是 de- 加 fungi（履行）：职责已完成，所以这东西结束了。

normal.en: Fungi means to perform a duty.
normal.cn: fungi 意为履行职责。

normal.en: De- means completely.
normal.cn: de- 表示彻底。

normal.en: Defunct means the duty is over.
normal.cn: defunct 意为职责已结束。

normal.en: A defunct factory has no shifts.
normal.cn: 停用的工厂没有排班。

normal.en: A defunct law binds nobody.
normal.cn: 废止的法律约束不了任何人。

abstract.en: A body whose work has stopped.
abstract.cn: 一具工作已经停下的身体。

abstract.en: A locked gate and an empty shift board.
abstract.cn: 一把锁住的门和一块空白的排班板。

abstract.en: A stamp cancelled with a line through it.
abstract.cn: 一枚被划了一道线的作废印章。

examples.en: The club has been defunct for years.
examples.cn: 这家俱乐部已经停办多年。

examples.en: They revived a defunct brand.
examples.cn: 他们复活了一个已消失的品牌。

examples.en: The treaty has been defunct since the war.
examples.cn: 战争之后这份条约已失效。

dict_mnemonic.text: defunct 谐音「弟方克特」——不如记 de（彻底）＋ funct（做，与 function 同根）＝该做的都做完了，「已死的、已废止的」。

root: 拉丁语 fungi（履行职责）→ defungi（彻底完成）→ defunctus（已完成、已死）→ 英语 defunct

sensesIntro.en: One finished duty: a body, a factory and a rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一份已完成的职责：一具身体、一家工厂与一条规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked factory gate with an empty shift board behind it
core.cn: 核心意象：一把锁住的工厂大门，门后是一块空白的排班板

branches.en: A body whose work has stopped.
branches.cn: 一具工作已经停下的身体。

branches.en: A locked gate and an empty shift board.
branches.cn: 一把锁住的门和一块空白的排班板。

branches.en: A stamp cancelled with a line through it.
branches.cn: 一枚被划了一道线的作废印章。

branches.en: Both name something whose activity has ended.
branches.cn: 两者都指活动已经结束的东西。

branches.en: Both are things people no longer rely on.
branches.cn: 两者都是人们不再依赖的东西。

intro.en: Defunct is de- plus fungi; the doing root builds the function family.
intro.cn: defunct 由 de- 加 fungi 构成；履行这个词根造出功能这一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fungi means to perform and abolere means to destroy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fungi 意为履行，abolere 意为废除。

definition_zh: v. 退化；堕落；变质 adj. 退化的；堕落的 n. 堕落者；退化者
definition_en: to become worse in quality or moral character; as an adjective, having lost good qualities; as a noun, a person who has lost moral standards
core_image: 一条原本清澈的溪流往下游走，越来越浑，最后成了泥沟
scene: 争论很快变成了辱骂。The debate degenerated into insults.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：degenerate 指质量或品格变坏；句意是争论很快沦为辱骂。

senses.title: Become worse in quality
senses.definition: to become worse in quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 质量或状况变差
senses.example: The debate degenerated into insults.
senses.exampleCN: 争论很快沦为辱骂。
senses.why: A clear stream turning to mud downstream.
senses.whyCN: 一条清溪往下游走成了泥沟。

senses.title: Fall in moral standards
senses.definition: to lose moral standards and behave badly
senses.definitionCN: 失去道德标准、行为变坏
senses.example: The regime degenerated into cruelty.
senses.exampleCN: 那个政权堕落成了残暴统治。
senses.why: A clean cloth stained by its own use.
senses.whyCN: 一块干净布被自己的使用弄脏。

senses.title: Having lost good qualities
senses.definition: having lost the qualities that were once good
senses.definitionCN: 已经失去原本良好品质的
senses.example: Degenerate cells no longer divide normally.
senses.exampleCN: 退化的细胞不再正常分裂。
senses.why: A copy whose lines have blurred.
senses.whyCN: 一份线条已经模糊的副本。

senses.title: A person who has fallen
senses.definition: a person who has lost moral standards
senses.definitionCN: 失去道德标准的人
senses.example: The paper called him a degenerate.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报纸称他为堕落者。
senses.why: A name given to someone who sank.
senses.whyCN: 给一个沉下去的人起的称呼。

intro.en: Degenerate comes from Latin degenerare, to fall from the kind of one birth, from de- plus genus.
intro.cn: degenerate 源自拉丁语 degenerare（背离本族），由 de- 加 genus（族、类）构成。

items.en: Genus meant race, kind or birth.
items.cn: genus 意为族、类或出身。

items.en: Degenerare meant to fall away from the kind of one birth.
items.cn: degenerare 意为背离自己的族类。

items.en: Degeneratus was the past participle.
items.cn: degeneratus 是其过去分词。

items.en: Degenerate entered English for falling from ancestral quality.
items.cn: 十六世纪 degenerate 以背离祖辈品质义进入英语。

items.en: Degenerate was used in biology and medicine.
items.cn: 十九世纪 degenerate 用于生物学与医学。

items.en: Degenerate became a strong moral insult.
items.cn: 二十世纪 degenerate 成为强烈的道德贬称。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the gen- birth family; the near-meaning group names getting worse.
note.cn: 形近组共享 gen-（出生）家族；近义组都是「变坏」的说法。

entries.definition: To produce or create something.
To grow or build again.
The process of becoming worse.
To become progressively worse.
To rot or fall into a worse state.
Dishonest or morally bad.
To lower in quality or dignity.

normalIntro.en: Degenerate is de- plus genus, kind: fall away from your own kind.
normalIntro.cn: degenerate 就是 de- 加 genus（族类）：从自己的族类上掉下来。

normal.en: Genus means kind or race.
normal.cn: genus 意为族类。

normal.en: De- means down or away.
normal.cn: de- 表示向下或离开。

normal.en: Degenerate falls below its kind.
normal.cn: degenerate 掉到本族水平之下。

normal.en: Generate builds up.
normal.cn: generate 是往上造。

normal.en: Degenerate runs down.
normal.cn: degenerate 是往下走。

abstract.en: A clear stream turning to mud downstream.
abstract.cn: 一条清溪往下游走成了泥沟。

abstract.en: A clean cloth stained by its own use.
abstract.cn: 一块干净布被自己的使用弄脏。

abstract.en: A copy whose lines have blurred.
abstract.cn: 一份线条已经模糊的副本。

examples.en: The protest degenerated into a riot.
examples.cn: 抗议演变成了骚乱。

examples.en: Doctors found degenerate tissue in the sample.
examples.cn: 医生在样本中发现了退化组织。

examples.en: He dismissed the idea as degenerate nonsense.
examples.cn: 他把这个想法斥为堕落的胡说。

dict_mnemonic.text: degenerate 谐音「弟詹纳瑞特」——不如记 de（向下）＋ gener（生，与 generate 同根）＋ ate＝生出来却往下走，「退化、堕落」。

root: 拉丁语 genus（族、类）→ degenerare（背离本族）→ degeneratus → 英语 degenerate

sensesIntro.en: One muddy stream: quality, morals, cells and a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一条变浑的溪：质量、道德、细胞与一个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear stream turning to mud as it runs downstream
core.cn: 核心意象：一条清溪往下游走，越来越浑，最后成了泥沟

branches.en: A clear stream turning to mud downstream.
branches.cn: 一条清溪往下游走成了泥沟。

branches.en: A clean cloth stained by its own use.
branches.cn: 一块干净布被自己的使用弄脏。

branches.en: A copy whose lines have blurred.
branches.cn: 一份线条已经模糊的副本。

branches.en: A name given to someone who sank.
branches.cn: 给一个沉下去的人起的称呼。

branches.en: All four are something that fell below the level of its kind.
branches.cn: 四者都是掉到本类水平之下的东西。

intro.en: Degenerate is de- plus genus; the birth root builds the generate and regenerate family.
intro.cn: degenerate 由 de- 加 genus 构成；出生这个词根造出产生与再生这一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus means kind and gignere means to beget.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 genus 意为族类，gignere 意为生育。

latinEntries.meaning: to fall from the kind of one birth

definition_zh: 退化；降解；品质下降；地位或尊严的降低
definition_en: the process of falling to a lower quality, condition, rank or structural state
core_image: 一块塑料样片在紫外灯下慢慢泛黄、开裂，最后一捏就碎
scene: 实验室的架子上，一块塑料样片在紫外灯下泛黄开裂，手指一捏就碎。Ultraviolet light caused degradation of the sample within weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 degradation 指「材料因光照、氧化等作用而逐渐失去原有性能」（第 4 个义项：材料退化与老化）；句意为紫外光在几周内使样片发生降解。图中可辨识物件：塑料样片、紫外灯、泛黄裂纹、碎屑。

pos.zh: 退化；降解；降级；品质或尊严的降低

senses.title: A general fall in quality or condition
senses.titleCN: 品质或状况的总体下降
senses.definition: the process by which something loses quality, value or good condition over time
senses.definitionCN: 某物随时间失去品质、价值或良好状态的过程
senses.example: Ultraviolet light caused degradation of the sample within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外光在几周内使样片发生降解。
senses.why: The word is de- 'down' plus gradus 'step', so degradation is a movement down one grade rather than a sudden collapse.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 de-「向下」加 gradus「台阶」，因此 degradation 是往下走一个等级，而非突然崩塌。

senses.title: Land and soil degradation
senses.definition: the loss of soil fertility, structure or cover through erosion, salinity, compaction or overuse
senses.definitionCN: 因侵蚀、盐渍化、压实或过度使用而失去肥力、结构或覆盖
senses.example: Continuous cropping sped up the degradation of the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 连作加快了山坡的退化。
senses.why: Soil is a slowly renewed body, so its degradation is measured in decades and is hard to reverse.
senses.whyCN: 土壤是缓慢更新的整体，其退化以十年计，且难以逆转。

senses.title: Chemical breakdown of a substance
senses.definition: the breaking of large molecules into smaller ones by heat, light, water or microbial action
senses.definitionCN: 大分子因热、光、水或微生物作用而断裂为较小分子
senses.example: The polymer's degradation released a faint acid smell.
senses.exampleCN: 这种聚合物的降解释放出一股淡淡的酸味。
senses.why: Chemistry uses the word for the loss of a molecule's structure, which is a literal stepping down of complexity.
senses.whyCN: 化学用这个词指分子结构的丧失，也就是复杂度的字面「降级」。

senses.title: Material degradation in service
senses.definition: the loss of strength, colour or function in a material through corrosion, wear, heat or radiation
senses.definitionCN: 材料因腐蚀、磨损、热或辐射而失去强度、颜色或功能
senses.example: Salt air caused steady degradation of the bridge cables.
senses.exampleCN: 含盐的海风使桥梁缆索持续退化。
senses.why: Engineering watches degradation as a rate, because safety depends on how fast a material steps down.
senses.whyCN: 工程把退化看作一个速率，因为安全取决于材料下降得多快。

senses.title: Social or moral debasement
senses.definition: the lowering of a person or group to a condition of humiliation, exploitation or loss of dignity
senses.definitionCN: 使人或群体陷入屈辱、剥削或失去尊严的状态
senses.example: The report described the degradation of workers in the camps.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了营地里工人所受的贬损。
senses.why: The word's oldest English sense is a falling from dignity, and it still carries moral weight.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的英语义项是「从尊严上跌落」，至今仍带道德分量。

senses.title: Ceremonial loss of rank
senses.definition: the formal stripping of a title, office or rank, once performed in public ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式剥夺头衔、职务或军阶，旧时在公开仪式中执行
senses.example: The old rite of degradation removed the knight's belt and spurs.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的降级礼卸下了骑士的腰带与马刺。
senses.why: This is the literal sense of de- plus gradus: a person is moved down a step of the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 这是 de- 加 gradus 的字面义：一个人被移下等级阶梯的一级。

senses.title: Habitat degradation in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中的栖息地退化
senses.definition: the loss of a habitat's structure and species composition while some of it remains
senses.definitionCN: 栖息地仍有部分留存，但其结构与物种组成已丧失
senses.example: Draining the marsh caused habitat degradation for nesting birds.
senses.exampleCN: 排干沼泽造成了营巢鸟类的栖息地退化。
senses.why: Ecology needs a word for partial loss, because a habitat can be ruined without being erased.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要一个词指「部分丧失」，因为栖息地可以已经被毁，却并未消失。

senses.title: Signal or data degradation
senses.definition: the loss of clarity, accuracy or resolution in a transmitted signal or stored dataset
senses.definitionCN: 传输信号或存储数据集在清晰度、准确度或分辨率上的损失
senses.example: Repeated copying caused degradation of the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 反复复制使这段录音出现劣化。
senses.why: Information theory borrowed the word because quality can step down through a chain without anything being added.
senses.whyCN: 信息论借用这个词，因为品质可以在一连串环节中下降，而并未添加任何东西。

senses.title: Abstract: erosion of institutional trust
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：制度与信任的侵蚀
senses.definition: a transferred use for the gradual weakening of standards, trust or co-operation in an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 转指组织内标准、信任或合作的逐渐削弱

intro.en: Degradation came to English from French and Latin, built on gradus 'step'. Its first English sense was a falling away from a former state, and the rank sense followed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: degradation 经法语与拉丁语进入英语，构自 gradus「台阶」。它最早的英语义项是「从原有状态跌落」，降级义随后出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gradus meant 'step, degree', from the verb gradi 'to walk'. The deeper origin of gradi is not established; the root commonly proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: gradus 意为「台阶、等级」，出自动词 gradi「行走」。gradi 的更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的词根是重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: De- 'down' plus gradus produced degradare 'to lower in rank', used first of clergy and officials moved down the hierarchy.
items.cn: de-「向下」加 gradus 构成 degradare「降低等级」，最初用于被移下等级的教士与官员。

items.en: Old French degradacion and English degradation appear in the fourteenth century with the sense of deterioration or degeneration, a falling from a former condition.
items.cn: 古法语 degradacion 与英语 degradation 在十四世纪出现，指恶化、变质，即从原有状态跌落。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word also named the public ceremony that stripped a knight or officer of rank.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词也指公开剥夺骑士或军官职级的仪式。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries chemistry, materials science and ecology adopted the word for the breakdown of substances, structures and habitats.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，化学、材料科学与生态学采用这个词来指物质、结构与栖息地的崩解。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of gradi, first date of the scientific sense): the walking root behind gradus is unsettled, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the chemical or ecological sense, so its date is approximate; any older form offered for gradi is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（gradi 的更深来源、科学义的首见年代）：gradus 背后「行走」的词根无定论，化学义与生态义的最早书证也无定论，年代只能约计；凡为 gradi 给出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same gradus stock that differ in grammar or sense; group two holds other words for falling quality, each stressing a different kind of loss.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 gradus 词干、语法或含义不同的词；第二组是其他表示品质下降的词，各自强调不同的损失。

entries.definition: To lower something in quality or rank; degradation is the process or result the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物品质或等级下降；degradation 是动词所产生过程或结果。

entries.definition: A series of steps or stages, from the same gradus root; it names an orderly scale, not a fall.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列台阶或阶段，同出 gradus 词根；它指有序的刻度，而非跌落。

entries.definition: Happening by small steps, from gradus; the adjective describes pace, not loss of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步发生的，出自 gradus；这个形容词描述节奏，而非品质损失。

entries.definition: To raise something to a higher grade; it reverses the de- of degradation while using the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物提升到更高等级；它与 degradation 的 de- 方向相反，却用同一词根。

entries.definition: Any worsening of condition; it is broader and less technical than degradation.
entries.definitionCN: 状况的任何恶化；它比 degradation 更宽泛、更少技术性。

entries.definition: Slow rotting or decomposition, especially of organic matter; degradation also covers metals, data and rank.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的腐烂或分解，尤指有机物；degradation 还涵盖金属、数据与等级。

entries.definition: The lowering of value, purity or dignity, as of coinage or character; it is a moral or monetary word.
entries.definitionCN: 价值、纯度或尊严的降低，如货币成色或人格；它是道德或货币领域的词。

entries.definition: Chemical attack on a metal surface; it is one cause of material degradation.
entries.definitionCN: 对金属表面的化学侵蚀；它是材料退化的一个原因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.

normal.en: De- 'down' plus gradus 'step': degradation is one step down the staircase.
normal.cn: de-「向下」加 gradus「台阶」：degradation 就是楼梯下了一级。

normal.en: The same root gives grade, gradual, graduate, upgrade and downgrade.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 grade、gradual、graduate、upgrade 与 downgrade。

normal.en: The family runs degrade, degraded, degradable, degradative and degradability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 degrade、degraded、degradable、degradative 与 degradability。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: land degradation, chemical degradation, material degradation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：土地退化、化学降解、材料退化。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was moral: a falling from dignity, not a falling of soil.
normal.cn: 最早的英语义项是道德性的：从尊严跌落，而非土壤流失。

examples.en: Land degradation lowered the yield of the whole district.
examples.cn: 土地退化降低了大片地区的产量。

examples.en: The term also names the degradation of a person's dignity.
examples.cn: 这个词也指一个人尊严的贬损。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one staircase: a higher condition exists, a step is taken downward, quality falls, structure breaks, standing falls, and finally the same image describes signals and institutions.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一段楼梯展开：本来处在较高状态，向下走一级，品质下降，结构断裂，地位跌落，最后同一意象描述信号与制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step worn lower than the one before it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一级比上一级磨得更低的台阶。

branches.en: GENERAL AND LAND: any quality can step down, and soil is the slowest case to repair.
branches.cn: 总体与土地：任何品质都能下台阶，土壤是最慢修复的一种。

branches.en: MATTER: molecules break apart and materials lose strength by the same downward movement.
branches.cn: 物质：分子断裂与材料失强，是同一种向下的运动。

branches.en: HUMAN STANDING: dignity and rank fall on the same scale as quality.
branches.cn: 人的地位：尊严与职级同品质一样沿同一尺度下落。

branches.en: HABITAT: a place can be degraded while still partly standing.
branches.cn: 栖息地：一个地方可以已经退化，却仍部分存在。

branches.en: TRANSFER: signals and trust lose resolution the way materials lose strength.
branches.cn: 转移：信号与信任失去清晰度，正如材料失去强度。

definition_zh: v. 使脱水；使干燥；（身体）失去水分
definition_en: to remove water from something, or to lose too much water from the body
core_image: 一排苹果片摆在暖烘干架上，水分一点点被逼出来，果子缩成薄片
scene: 长途飞行让他严重缺水。The long flight dehydrated him badly.

pos.zh: 使脱水；使干燥；（身体）失去水分

senses.title: Remove water from food
senses.definition: to take the water out of food so that it keeps longer
senses.definitionCN: 把食物里的水分去掉，以便保存更久
senses.example: They dehydrate the fruit before packing it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在包装前把水果脱水。
senses.why: Slices shrinking on a warm drying rack.
senses.whyCN: 暖烘干架上正在缩小的薄片。

senses.title: Dry out a surface
senses.definition: to make skin, soil or air lose its moisture
senses.definitionCN: 使皮肤、土壤或空气失去水分
senses.example: The heater dehydrates the air in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 暖气使房间里的空气变干。
senses.why: A cracked lip beside a dry radiator.
senses.whyCN: 干裂的嘴唇挨着一台干燥的暖气片。

senses.title: Lose body water
senses.definition: to lose more fluid from the body than is taken in
senses.definitionCN: 身体流失的水分多于摄入的水分
senses.example: The long flight dehydrated him badly.
senses.exampleCN: 长途飞行让他严重脱水。
senses.why: A runner sweating without a water bottle.
senses.whyCN: 一个出汗却没带水壶的跑者。

intro.en: Dehydrate is de-, removal, plus hydrate, from Greek hydōr, water.
intro.cn: dehydrate 由 de-（去除）加 hydrate（水合物）构成，后者源自希腊语 hydōr（水）。

items.en: Hydōr meant water in Greek.
items.cn: 希腊语 hydōr 意为水。

items.en: Hydrate named a compound holding water.
items.cn: hydrate 指含水的化合物。

items.en: Dehydrate was formed for removing that water.
items.cn: dehydrate 被造出来表示去掉这些水。

items.en: Doctors used it for patients losing fluid.
items.cn: 医生用它描述体液流失的病人。

items.en: Dried milk and vegetables put it on labels.
items.cn: 奶粉与脱水蔬菜让它印上包装标签。

items.en: It now covers sport, skin care and camping food.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖运动、护肤与露营食品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the hydr- water family; the near-meaning group names ways of making things dry.
note.cn: 形近组共享 hydr-（水）家族；近义组都是「弄干」的说法。

examples.cn: 在山路上脱水之前先喝水。

definition_zh: 推迟；耽搁；延迟
definition_en: to make something happen later than planned, or the time lost by waiting
core_image: 站台上的人群一起抬头看晚点的牌子
scene: 大雪压住了铁轨，清晨的列车一班接一班停在站外。Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
sceneCN: 这里 delay 指「耽搁」（第 1 个义项：使事情比计划更晚发生）；句意是大雪让早班列车晚点。

senses.title: Make it happen later
senses.definition: to arrange for something to take place at a later time
senses.definitionCN: 把某事安排到更晚的时间进行
senses.example: They delayed the meeting until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议推迟到星期五。
senses.why: A thing put off is a thing still waiting on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 被推迟的事，就是还搁在架子上等着的。

senses.title: Hold someone up on the way
senses.definition: to make a person or vehicle late by slowing them down
senses.definitionCN: 因拖慢速度而使人或车辆迟到
senses.example: Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪让早班列车晚点。
senses.why: One slow point on a road makes every traveller late.
senses.whyCN: 路上一个慢下来的地方，就让所有赶路的人迟到。

senses.title: The time lost in waiting
senses.definition: the period of waiting caused by something being late
senses.definitionCN: 因某事迟到而产生的等待时间
senses.example: There was a delay of two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 延误了两个小时。
senses.why: Waiting is the shape that lost time takes in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 等待，就是失去的时间在心里留下的形状。

intro.en: Delay comes from Old French delaier, to put off, built on Latin laxare, to loosen.
intro.cn: delay 来自古法语 delaier（往后放），底层是拉丁语 laxare（放松、松开）。

items.en: Laxare meant to loosen a hold or a rope.
items.cn: laxare 意为把抓住的手或绳子松开。

items.en: Delaier joined de- with laier, to leave something for later.
items.cn: delaier 由 de- 与 laier 合成，意为留到以后再说。

items.en: English used delay for both putting off and being held up.
items.cn: 英语用它既指主动推迟，也指被动耽搁。

items.en: The noun delay settled into talk of journeys and courts.
items.cn: 名词用法在旅途与法庭的说法里安定下来。

items.en: Trains, flights and replies are all said to be delayed.
items.cn: 如今列车、航班和回复都可以说被延误。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ay ending, and the meaning group names three ways of making something wait.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ay 这个尾巴，近义组则是三种让人或事等一等的方式。

entries.definition: to pass a message or signal on
to be slowly destroyed by natural causes
to make a fear or worry less strong
to move an event to a later date
entries.definitionCN: 把活动改到更晚的日期

entries.definition: to decide to do something later
to stop something from moving on time

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a crowd looking up at a board and end with two hours that simply vanished.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一群人抬头看牌子开始，落到凭空消失的两个小时。

normal.en: A train is late once, but the waiting is repeated by everyone.
normal.cn: 列车只晚一次，等待却被每个人各经历一遍。

normal.en: Delay is not a stop; the wheels are still turning, only slower.
normal.cn: 耽搁不是停下，轮子还在转，只是慢了。

normal.en: The meeting moved by two days costs two days of guessing.
normal.cn: 会议挪两天，就多出两天猜测。

normal.en: To delay a reply is to say nothing in a loud way.
normal.cn: 拖着不回，就是用很响的方式什么也不说。

normal.en: Relay passes a message on; delay keeps it back.
normal.cn: relay 把消息传下去，delay 把消息留住。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with one hand moving slower than the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，一根针走得比另一根慢。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that does not move but grows.
abstract.cn: 想象一支不往前挪、却越来越长的队伍。

abstract.en: Picture a letter left in a drawer for a week.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信在抽屉里躺了一星期。

examples.en: Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
examples.cn: 大雪让早班列车晚点。

examples.en: They delayed the meeting until Friday.
examples.cn: 他们把会议推迟到星期五。

examples.en: There was a delay of two hours.
examples.cn: 延误了两个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delay 记成「地雷」：路上踩到地雷，队伍就走不动，只好延误。

root: 来自古法语 delaier（留到以后），其底层是拉丁语 laxare（松开），本义是把抓着的事放开、让它往后滑。它先指主动推迟，后来也指被动耽搁，如今连列车、航班与回复晚到都用它。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan moved forward on the calendar, to a train held in the snow, to the empty hours that remain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从日历上往后挪的计划，到被雪挡住的列车，再到剩下那几个空掉的小时。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a station board where one line turns late.
core.cn: 核心意象：车站牌上有一行变成了晚点。

branches.en: The first sense moves the agreed time further on.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把商定的时间往后挪。

branches.en: The second sense is being slowed on the way.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是在路上被拖慢。

branches.en: The third sense is the waiting that results.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是由此产生的等待。

branches.en: A choice and an accident produce the same lateness.
branches.cn: 主动的选择与被动的意外，造成同一种晚。

branches.en: The train and the empty hour are one event seen twice.
branches.cn: 晚点的列车与空掉的一小时，是同一件事的两面。

intro.en: Delay forms a few adjectives and nouns, all about lateness and waiting.
intro.cn: delay 能派生出几个形容词与名词，全都与晚点和等待有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is laxare, to loosen, with de- giving the sense of away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 laxare（松开），前缀 de- 带来「离开」的意味。

items.meaning: to put off, or the wait
items.example: The delay was caused by fog.
The delayed train arrived at noon.
A delaying tactic bought them a day.
items.exampleCN: 拖延的办法为他们争到一天。

items.example: He was the delayer of every plan.
items.exampleCN: 每个计划都是他拖下来的。

items.example: A long delay tested our patience.
items.exampleCN: 漫长的延误考验了我们的耐性。

items.meaning: a gap between act and result
items.example: There is a short time delay in the signal.

definition_zh: 代表；委派；授权
definition_en: a person sent to speak for a group; also to give a task or power to someone else
core_image: 一个人举起写着团体名字的牌子
scene: 会议开始前，每个人在门口的册子上写下自己的名字和所代表的城市。Each delegate signed the book at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 delegate 指「代表」（第 1 个义项：替团体出席的人）；句意是每位代表都在门口册子上签了名。

senses.title: A person who speaks for a group
senses.definition: someone chosen to attend a meeting and act for a larger group
senses.definitionCN: 被选去参加会议并代表较大团体行事的人
senses.example: Each delegate signed the book at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 每位代表都在门口册子上签了名。
senses.why: A crowd cannot all stand at one table, so it sends one pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 一群人没法都坐到同一张桌前，只好派出一双手。

senses.title: Hand a task to someone
senses.definition: to give part of one's work to another person to do
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的一部分工作交给别人去做
senses.example: A good manager delegates the small tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 好的管理者会把小事分派出去。
senses.why: Two hands can hold more than one pair can.
senses.whyCN: 两双手能拿的东西，比一双手多。

senses.title: Give power to another
senses.definition: to give someone the right to act or decide in your place
senses.definitionCN: 授予他人代替你行事或决定的权力
senses.example: The board delegated full power to the new director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会把全部权力授予了新主管。
senses.why: Trust is a key that changes hands without changing locks.
senses.whyCN: 信任是一把换了手、却没换锁的钥匙。

intro.en: Delegate comes from Latin delegare, to send with a charge, from de- away and legare to send.
intro.cn: delegate 来自拉丁语 delegare（派人带任务去），由 de-（离开）与 legare（派遣）组成。

items.en: Legare meant to send a person with a duty.
items.cn: legare 意为派一个人带着任务去。

items.en: Delegare added the idea of handing the charge over.
items.cn: delegare 又多了一层「把任务交出去」的意思。

items.en: English used delegate as a noun for a sent person.
items.cn: 英语先把 delegate 作名词，指被派出去的人。

items.en: The verb grew, meaning to entrust work or power.
items.cn: 动词用法长出来，指托付工作或权力。

items.en: Managers now delegate tasks as easily as states send delegates.
items.cn: 如今管理者分派任务，就像国家派出代表一样自然。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the leg stem, and the meaning group names the person who stands in for others.
note.cn: 形近组共用 leg 词干，近义组则是几个「替别人出面」的人。

entries.definition: a group sent to speak for others
entries.definitionCN: 被派去代表他人发言的一群人

entries.definition: done on purpose and after thought
an official messenger of high rank
a person chosen to act for a group
entries.definitionCN: 被选来代表团体行事的人

entries.definition: a person who acts for a leader
a person sent to carry a message

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a name written at a meeting door and end with a key handed to someone you trust.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从会议门口写下的名字开始，落到交到信任之人手里的钥匙。

normal.en: One person at the table can carry a whole town in a folder.
normal.cn: 桌边一个人，文件夹里能装下一整座城。

normal.en: A manager who keeps every task ends up holding nothing well.
normal.cn: 什么活都攥在手里的管理者，最后什么也拿不稳。

normal.en: To delegate is to lend your signature for a while.
normal.cn: 授权，就是把自己的签名借出去一阵。

normal.en: A delegate is a voice sent away from home.
normal.cn: 代表，是从家里被派出去的一个声音。

normal.en: Legare means to send, so a delegate is one who was sent.
normal.cn: legare 是派遣，所以代表就是被派出去的人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised with a card bearing a town's name.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起来，牌子上写着一座城的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of papers moving from one desk to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠纸从一张桌子移到另一张桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a key pressed into a palm and the fingers closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙按进掌心，手指合拢。

examples.en: Each delegate signed the book at the door.
examples.cn: 每位代表都在门口册子上签了名。

examples.en: A good manager delegates the small tasks.
examples.cn: 好的管理者会把小事分派出去。

examples.en: The board delegated full power to the new director.
examples.cn: 董事会把全部权力授予了新主管。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delegate 记成「得力干将」：de 开头，legate 是派出去的人，派出去的总是得力的那位。

root: 源自拉丁语 delegare，由 de-（离开）与 legare（派遣）合成，本义是派人带着任务出去。英语先把它作名词表示使者与代表，十六世纪又生出动词义，指把工作或权力托付给别人。

sensesIntro.en: From a person sent to a meeting, to a task handed over, to the right to decide in your place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被派去开会的人，到交出去的一项工作，再到代你决定的权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pair of hands holding a card for many people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手替许多人举着一块牌子。

branches.en: The first sense is the chosen person who speaks for the rest.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是被选中替众人说话的人。

branches.en: The second sense is work passed to another pair of hands.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把工作交到另一双手里。

branches.en: The third sense lends the right to decide, not only the work.
branches.cn: 第三个义项借出的是决定权，不只是活儿。

branches.en: A representative and a handed task are both things sent outward.
branches.cn: 代表与被交出的任务，都是被送出去的东西。

branches.en: Both senses trust another person with a part of your own role.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把自己角色的一部分托付给别人。

intro.en: Delegate brings nouns of groups and of the act of handing power over.
intro.cn: delegate 带来表示团体和授权行为的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is legare, to send, with de- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 legare（派遣），前缀 de- 表示离开。

items.example: One delegate spoke for the village.

items.meaning: a group sent, or the act of entrusting
items.example: A small delegation met the mayor.
items.exampleCN: 一个小代表团见了市长。

items.example: The delegated work was finished early.
items.exampleCN: 分派出去的工作提前完成了。

items.meaning: the one who hands work over
items.example: The delegator keeps the final say.
items.exampleCN: 委派者保留最后决定权。

items.meaning: able to be handed to another
items.exampleCN: 并非每项职责都能交出去。

items.meaning: a person sent to discuss trade
items.example: The trade delegate met the exporters.
items.exampleCN: 贸易代表会见了出口商。
好的领导者会下放权力。

items.meaning: a person attending a conference for a group
items.example: Every conference delegate got a badge.
items.exampleCN: 每位会议代表都领到了胸牌。

definition_zh: n. 删除；删去；被删掉的部分；（基因）缺失
definition_en: the act of removing something written or stored, or a part that has been lost

pos.zh: 删除；删去；被删掉的部分；（基因）缺失

senses.title: Act of removing text
senses.definition: the act of taking out words, lines or files
senses.definitionCN: 去掉字词、行或文件的动作
senses.example: The deletion shortened the report by two pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这处删除让报告短了两页。
senses.why: A red line through a sentence on a proof.
senses.whyCN: 校样上一句被红线划掉的话。

senses.title: The part removed
senses.definition: the words or data that have been taken out
senses.definitionCN: 已被去掉的文字或数据
senses.example: Restore the deletion from the backup.
senses.exampleCN: 从备份里恢复被删掉的内容。
senses.why: An empty slot where a paragraph used to sit.

senses.title: Missing genetic piece
senses.definition: the loss of a section of DNA or of a chromosome
senses.definitionCN: DNA 或染色体上一段的丢失
senses.example: The test found a small gene deletion.
senses.exampleCN: 检测发现一处小的基因缺失。
senses.why: A ladder with one rung taken away.
senses.whyCN: 一架被抽掉一根横档的梯子。

intro.en: Deletion comes from Latin delere, to destroy or erase, through the noun deletio.
intro.cn: deletion 源自拉丁语 delere（毁灭、抹去），经名词 deletio 而来。

items.en: Delere meant to destroy or wipe out.
items.cn: delere 意为毁灭或抹去。

items.en: Deletio named the act of wiping out.
items.cn: deletio 指抹去这一行为。

items.en: Deletion entered English for striking out text.
items.cn: 十六世纪 deletion 以划掉文字义进入英语。

items.en: Editors used it for cuts in a manuscript.
items.cn: 编辑用它指手稿上的删节。

items.en: It became the standard word for removing files.
items.cn: 它成为删除文件的标准说法。

items.en: Deletion named a lost stretch of DNA.
items.cn: deletion 指丢失的一段 DNA。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the del- wiping family; the near-meaning group names other kinds of taking away.
note.cn: 形近组共享 del-（抹去）家族；近义组是其他「拿走」的说法。

entries.definition: To take out text or data.
Causing harm or damage.
A belief that is not true.
The act of taking something away.
The act of rubbing out marks.
Something left out or not done.

normalIntro.en: Deletion is delete plus -ion: the thing you do when you wipe a line out.
normalIntro.cn: deletion 就是 delete 加 -ion：你把一行字抹掉时做的那件事。

normal.en: Delete means to wipe out.
normal.cn: delete 意为抹去。

normal.en: -ion turns a verb into a noun.
normal.cn: -ion 把动词变成名词。

normal.en: A deletion leaves a gap.
normal.cn: 一处删除留下一个空缺。

normal.en: Accidental deletions can be undone.
normal.cn: 误删可以撤销。

normal.en: A gene deletion loses a rung of DNA.
normal.cn: 基因缺失丢掉一段 DNA。

abstract.en: A red line through a sentence on a proof.
abstract.cn: 校样上一句被红线划掉的话。

abstract.en: An empty slot where a paragraph used to sit.

abstract.en: A ladder with one rung taken away.
abstract.cn: 一架被抽掉一根横档的梯子。

examples.en: Accidental deletions can be undone.
examples.cn: 误删是可以撤销的。

examples.en: The deletion of the clause changed the meaning.
examples.cn: 删掉这一条款改变了含义。

examples.en: She marked every deletion in red ink.
examples.cn: 她用红笔标出每一处删除。

dict_mnemonic.text: deletion ＝ delete（删除）＋ -ion（名词后缀）。delete 源自拉丁语 delere（抹去），所以「抹掉这件事」就是 deletion，既指删除动作，也指被删掉的缺口。

root: 拉丁语 delere（抹去）→ deletio（抹去的行为）→ 英语 delete（删除）＋ -ion → deletion

sensesIntro.en: One thing taken out: a sentence, a file and a rung of DNA.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一样被拿走的东西：一句话、一个文件与一段 DNA。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line through a sentence, leaving an empty slot on the proof
core.cn: 核心意象：校样上一句被红线划掉，留下一个空位

branches.en: A red line through a sentence on a proof.
branches.cn: 校样上一句被红线划掉的话。

branches.en: Both concern text that is no longer there.
branches.cn: 两者都关乎已经不在了的文字。

branches.en: Both name a missing piece rather than an act.
branches.cn: 两者都指缺失的部分，而非动作。

intro.en: Deletion is delete plus -ion; the wiping root also builds the removal family.
intro.cn: deletion 由 delete 加 -ion 构成；抹去这个词根也造出移除一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin delere means to wipe out, radere to scrape and mittere to send.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 delere 意为抹去，radere 意为刮，mittere 意为送。

definition_zh: 故意的；从容的；仔细考虑
definition_en: done on purpose after thinking; slow and calm; also to think something over carefully
core_image: 一双手把两样东西放在天平两端慢慢比较
scene: 十二个人在屋里坐了很久，桌上的纸翻了又翻，谁也没有先开口。The jury deliberated for three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 deliberate 指「仔细考虑」（第 3 个义项：反复权衡后作出判断）；句意是陪审团商议了三个小时。

senses.title: Done on purpose
senses.definition: planned and intended rather than accidental
senses.definitionCN: 有计划有意图的，而非偶然发生的
senses.example: The mistake was not deliberate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个错误不是故意的。
senses.why: What is weighed before it is done leaves a mark of choice.
senses.whyCN: 做之前先称量过的事，会留下选择的痕迹。

senses.title: Slow and unhurried
senses.definition: moving or speaking slowly and in a calm, steady way
senses.definitionCN: 动作或说话缓慢、平稳而不慌
senses.example: He crossed the room with deliberate steps.
senses.exampleCN: 他以不慌不忙的脚步穿过房间。
senses.why: A person who is thinking does not want to arrive too soon.
senses.whyCN: 正在思考的人，不想太早到达。

senses.title: Weigh a matter in council
senses.definition: to discuss and think about a question carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定前就一个问题仔细讨论与思考
senses.example: The jury deliberated for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团商议了三个小时。
senses.why: Two sides of a question are two pans that must be let settle.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题有两面，就像天平的两个盘，要让它慢慢稳下来。

intro.en: Deliberate comes from Latin deliberare, to weigh well, from de- and libra, a balance.
intro.cn: deliberate 来自拉丁语 deliberare（好好称量），由 de- 与 libra（天平）组成。

items.en: Libra was the scale on which goods were weighed.
items.cn: libra 是称货用的天平。

items.en: Deliberare meant to hold a question in the balance.
items.cn: deliberare 意为把一个问题放到天平上称。

items.en: English took the verb for thinking a matter over.
items.cn: 英语借来这个动词，表示反复思量一件事。

items.en: The adjective added the sense of a calm, slow manner.
items.cn: 形容词用法又添了从容、缓慢的意味。

items.en: Today a deliberate act is one nobody can call careless.
items.cn: 如今一个故意的行为，就是谁也不能说它粗心。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deli- opening, and the meaning group moves from intended to unhurried.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deli- 开头，近义组则从有意一路走到不慌不忙。

entries.definition: long and careful discussion
needing gentle and careful handling
a person sent to act for a group
done because one means to do it
thought out before it happens
entries.definitionCN: 在发生之前就已想好的

entries.definition: moving without any rush

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two pans of a balance and end with steps that never hurry.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从天平的两个盘开始，落到从不着急的脚步。

normal.en: A choice that was weighed has a different weight in the hand.
normal.cn: 称过的选择，拿在手里的分量不一样。

normal.en: A slow walk across a room says more than a quick word.
normal.cn: 慢慢走过一间屋子，比一句快话更能说明问题。

normal.en: Twelve people in one room are twelve balances, all waiting.
normal.cn: 一屋十二个人，就是十二架天平，一起等着。

normal.en: An accident leaves no plan behind; a deliberate act does.
normal.cn: 意外不留计划，故意的行为会留下。

normal.en: Libra is a balance, so to deliberate is to let the pans settle.
normal.cn: libra 是天平，所以商议就是让两个盘慢慢稳下来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a scale perfectly level.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把天平端得平平的。

abstract.en: Picture a foot placed down heel first, then toe.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚先落脚跟，再落脚尖。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs and one sheet of paper moving between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子，一张纸在中间传来传去。

examples.en: The jury deliberated for three hours.
examples.cn: 陪审团商议了三个小时。

examples.en: The mistake was not deliberate.
examples.cn: 这个错误不是故意的。

examples.en: He crossed the room with deliberate steps.
examples.cn: 他以不慌不忙的脚步穿过房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deliberate 记成「地里拨来拨去」：先掂量再动手，就是反复考虑；掂量过的举动，就是故意的。

root: 源自拉丁语 deliberare，词根 libra 是称货用的天平，本义是把一个问题放到天平上称一称。称量要慢，所以它既指「反复考虑」，也指考虑过后有意的举动，还引申出不慌不忙的姿态。

sensesIntro.en: From a question held in a balance, to a choice made with open eyes, to a walk that refuses to hurry.
sensesIntro.cn: 从放在天平上的问题，到睁着眼作出的选择，再到不肯着急的脚步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pans of a balance slowly coming level.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平的两个盘慢慢平下来。

branches.en: The first sense is an act that came out of a choice.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是从选择里长出来的行为。

branches.en: The second sense keeps the slow pace of weighing.
branches.cn: 第二个义项保留了称量时那种慢。

branches.en: The third sense is the weighing itself, done aloud in a group.
branches.cn: 第三个义项就是称量本身，在一群人里说出来。

branches.en: A purpose and a discussion are the two ends of one process.
branches.cn: 目的与商议，是同一个过程的两头。

branches.en: Both senses treat time as something worth spending.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把时间当成值得花的东西。

intro.en: Deliberate has a family of adverbs and nouns about thinking before acting.
intro.cn: deliberate 有一族副词与名词，都与「先想再做」有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is libra, a balance, with de- giving a sense of thoroughness.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 libra（天平），前缀 de- 带来彻底的意味。

items.example: She deliberately left the door open.

items.exampleCN: 商议很久之后他们同意了。

items.example: The council is a deliberative body.
items.exampleCN: 这个委员会是审议机构。

items.example: The deliberateness of the act was clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个行为的有意十分明显。
他们就这个计划进行了商议。

items.example: The work went on at deliberate speed.
items.exampleCN: 工作以从容的速度推进。

items.example: It was a deliberate attempt to mislead.

definition_zh: 易碎的；精致的；微妙的
definition_en: easily broken or harmed; finely made; needing careful handling
core_image: 薄胎瓷碗托在掌心，手指不敢用力
scene: 她托着那只薄薄的杯子，走路时连呼吸都放轻了。She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
sceneCN: 这里 delicate 指「易碎的」（第 1 个义项：容易碰坏）；句意是她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。

senses.title: Easily broken or hurt
senses.definition: thin or weak enough to be damaged with little force
senses.definitionCN: 薄或弱到稍一用力就会损坏
senses.example: She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
senses.exampleCN: 她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。
senses.why: What is lovely is often what breaks first.
senses.whyCN: 好看的东西，往往最先坏。

senses.title: Finely made and pleasing
senses.definition: made with fine skill and a light, careful touch
senses.definitionCN: 以精细手艺和轻巧手法做成
senses.example: The box was carved with a delicate pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子上刻着精致的花纹。
senses.why: Thin lines take longer to cut, and the eye knows it.
senses.whyCN: 细线要花更久去刻，眼睛看得出这份工夫。

senses.title: Needing careful handling
senses.definition: sensitive and easy to upset, of a matter or situation
senses.definitionCN: 指事情或处境敏感，容易被打乱
senses.example: The two countries kept a delicate balance.
senses.exampleCN: 两国之间维持着微妙的平衡。
senses.why: Some things are held together by almost nothing.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西，几乎只靠一点点力气才没有散。

intro.en: Delicate comes from Latin delicatus, which first meant giving pleasure and then finely made.
intro.cn: delicate 来自拉丁语 delicatus，先指令人愉悦，再指做得精细。

items.en: Delicatus described something that delighted the senses.
items.cn: delicatus 形容让感官愉悦的东西。

items.en: Over time it came to mean fine, soft and easily harmed.
items.cn: 后来它又指纤细、柔软、容易受损。

items.en: English used it for fine cloth, food and health.
items.cn: 英语用它形容精细的布、食物和身体。

items.en: The word moved from the body to matters of feeling and politics.
items.cn: 这个词从身体一路挪到情感与政治。

items.en: A delicate matter is one handled with words instead of hands.
items.cn: 如今微妙的事，要用言语而不是手去托。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deli- opening, and the meaning group moves from breakable to fine to tricky.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deli- 开头，近义组则从易碎走到精细再到棘手。

entries.definition: to give time or effort to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 把时间或精力献给某个目的

entries.definition: a person sent to act for a group
a rare and pleasing food
easily broken
very thin or made with great skill
not obvious and needing care to notice
entries.definitionCN: 不明显、需要细心才能察觉的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thin cup in two hands and end with two countries standing very still.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从双手托着的一只薄杯开始，落到两个一动不动站着的国家。

normal.en: The thinner the cup, the more the hand must listen.
normal.cn: 杯子越薄，手越要会听。

normal.en: Fine lines are slow lines, and the eye pays for them.
normal.cn: 细线都是慢线，眼睛是愿意为此付钱的。

normal.en: A flower proves nothing about strength, only about care.
normal.cn: 花不证明力量，只证明有人肯小心。

normal.en: A delicate balance is not a balance that stays by itself.
normal.cn: 微妙的平衡，不是自己会保持的平衡。

normal.en: Delicacy of taste and delicacy of skin share one skin-thin idea.
normal.cn: 口味的细腻与皮肤的娇嫩，共享同一个「薄」的念头。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip moving a hair off a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖把一根头发从纸上捻走。

abstract.en: Picture lace held up against a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一片蕾丝举在窗前。

abstract.en: Picture two glass balls touching and neither breaking.
abstract.cn: 想象两个玻璃球轻轻相触，谁也没碎。

examples.en: She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
examples.cn: 她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。

examples.en: The box was carved with a delicate pattern.
examples.cn: 盒子上刻着精致的花纹。

examples.en: The two countries kept a delicate balance.
examples.cn: 两国之间维持着微妙的平衡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delicate 记成「得立刻特小心」：薄得一碰就坏，所以得立刻特别小心。

root: 源自拉丁语 delicatus，本义是令人愉悦、讨人喜欢，后来添上纤细、柔软、容易受损的意思。经法语进入英语后，它从布料、食物与身体，一路扩展到情感与局势，于是易碎、精致、微妙三层意思并存。

sensesIntro.en: From a cup that breaks, to work that took great skill, to a balance nobody dares disturb.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一碰就碎的杯子，到极费手艺的活计，再到谁也不敢碰的平衡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin-walled cup held in two careful hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手小心托着一只薄壁杯子。

branches.en: The first sense is thinness that breaks under little force.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是稍一用力就坏的薄。

branches.en: The second sense is thinness used as skill and beauty.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把薄做成了手艺与美。

branches.en: The third sense is thinness in a situation, where one word can tip it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是处境的薄，一句话就能打破。

branches.en: What is finely made is also what needs care to keep.
branches.cn: 做得精细的东西，也需要小心才留得住。

branches.en: Both senses praise a thing that cannot be handled roughly.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说：这东西经不起粗手粗脚。

intro.en: Delicate has nouns and adverbs about fineness, and the noun delicacy carries both taste and care.
intro.cn: delicate 有表示精细的名词与副词，其中 delicacy 既有美味，也有分寸。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is delicatus, pleasing and fine, from deliciae, delight.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 delicatus（悦人而精细），出自 deliciae（愉悦）。

items.meaning: a rare food, or fineness of touch
items.example: The fish is a local delicacy.
The delicateness of the bowl surprised me.
The lake keeps a delicate balance.
items.exampleCN: 这片湖维持着微妙的平衡。

items.example: Money is a delicate issue here.
items.exampleCN: 钱在这里是个敏感话题。

items.example: The tea has a delicate taste.

definition_zh: 欣喜；乐事；使高兴
definition_en: great pleasure; something that gives pleasure; to give someone great pleasure
core_image: 孩子看见第一场雪，原地跳了起来
scene: 雪刚落下薄薄一层，孩子们冲到院子里，笑声撞在墙上。The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
sceneCN: 这里 delight 指「欣喜」（第 1 个义项：极大的愉快）；句意是初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。

senses.title: A rush of great pleasure
senses.definition: a strong feeling of happiness and enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而明亮的快乐感受
senses.example: The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。
senses.why: Joy that arrives suddenly comes out as a sound, not a word.
senses.whyCN: 突然到来的快乐，是先从声音里出来的，不是从词里。

senses.title: Something that gives joy
senses.definition: a person or thing that brings great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 带来极大快乐的人或事物
senses.example: The garden is her greatest delight.
senses.exampleCN: 花园是她最大的乐趣。
senses.why: We name the source with the same word as the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 我们把源头和感受，用同一个词来叫。

senses.title: Give someone joy
senses.definition: to please someone greatly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人非常高兴
senses.example: The small band delighted the whole hall.
senses.exampleCN: 这支小乐队让全场都很高兴。
senses.why: A pleasure that can be given away doubles itself.
senses.whyCN: 能送出去的快乐，会变成两份。

intro.en: Delight comes from Latin delectare, to charm, through Old French delit, which English respelled with gh.
intro.cn: delight 来自拉丁语 delectare（使着迷），经古法语 delit 进入英语，后来才拼上 gh。

items.en: Delectare meant to draw someone in with charm.
items.cn: delectare 意为用魅力把人吸引过来。

items.en: Delectatio named the pleasure that followed.
items.cn: delectatio 指随之而来的愉悦。

items.en: Delit kept the sense of a sweet enjoyment.
items.cn: delit 保留了甜美享受的意思。

items.en: English writers added gh, perhaps by confusion with light.
items.cn: 英语写作者加上 gh，可能是受了 light 的影响。

items.en: The word now covers both the feeling and its cause.
items.cn: 如今它既指感受，也指引起感受的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the light ending, and the meaning group moves from joy to the act of pleasing.
note.cn: 形近组绕着 light 这个尾巴，近义组则从快乐走到使人快乐。

entries.definition: very pleasing
the natural light of the sun
very good to eat
a deep feeling of happiness
a feeling of being pleased
to make someone happy

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with children in the first snow and end with a small band making a hall smile.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从初雪里的孩子开始，落到让整座大厅都笑起来的小乐队。

normal.en: The first snow is not a thing but a reason to shout.
normal.cn: 初雪不是一样东西，而是一个喊出来的理由。

normal.en: A garden can be a friend you water.
normal.cn: 一座花园，可以是你浇过水的朋友。

normal.en: What you take delight in, you will find time for.
normal.cn: 你以之为乐的事，总能腾出时间。

normal.en: To delight others is to hand them a small holiday.
normal.cn: 让别人高兴，就是递给对方一个小小的假日。

normal.en: Someone put gh into delight to make it look like light.
normal.cn: 有人往 delight 里塞进 gh，让它看着像 light。

abstract.en: Picture a boot making the first mark in fresh snow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只靴子在新雪上踩出第一个印。

abstract.en: Picture a face that cannot stop smiling at nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一张对着空气也止不住笑的脸。

abstract.en: Picture hands clapping before the song has ended.
abstract.cn: 想象歌还没唱完，掌声就起来了。

examples.en: The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
examples.cn: 初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。

examples.en: The garden is her greatest delight.
examples.cn: 花园是她最大的乐趣。

examples.en: The small band delighted the whole hall.
examples.cn: 这支小乐队让全场都很高兴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delight 记成「地来特」：好事落到地上来，心里一下亮起来，就是欣喜。

root: 源自拉丁语 delectare（以魅力吸引），名词 delectatio 指随之而来的愉悦；经古法语 delit 进入英语，拼写上加了 gh，可能受了 light 的影响。它同时保留了感受、来源与动作三层意思：欣喜、乐事、使高兴。

sensesIntro.en: From a shout in the snow, to the garden that caused it, to the band that caused the shout.
sensesIntro.cn: 从雪地里的一声喊，到引起这声喊的花园，再到让全场喊起来的那支乐队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child jumping in the first snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子在初雪里蹦起来。

branches.en: The first sense is the lifted feeling itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那种被抬起来的感受。

branches.en: The second sense is the thing that lifted it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把心抬起来的那样东西。

branches.en: The third sense is doing that lifting for someone else.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是替别人把心抬起来。

branches.en: Feeling and cause are one word because they arrive together.
branches.cn: 感受与原因共用一个词，因为它们总是一起到。

branches.en: What delights us can be passed on to others.
branches.cn: 让我们高兴的东西，也可以传给旁人。

intro.en: Delight grows adjectives of joy and adverbs of charm, all from the same Latin root.
intro.cn: delight 长出表示高兴的形容词与表示迷人的副词，都出自同一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is delectare, to charm, from lacere, to lure.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 delectare（使着迷），出自 lacere（引诱）。

items.example: Her face was full of delight.

items.exampleCN: 听到这个消息我们很高兴。

items.example: The delightfulness of the place stayed with us.
items.exampleCN: 那地方的可爱一直留在我们心里。

items.example: To our delight, the sun came out.
items.exampleCN: 让我们高兴的是，太阳出来了。

intro.en: Delineate comes from Latin delineare, de- plus lineare, to draw lines, from linea, a linen thread.
intro.cn: delineate 源自拉丁语 delineare，由 de- 加 lineare（画线）构成，linea 原指亚麻线。

items.en: Linea meant a linen thread, and then a line.
items.cn: linea 原指亚麻线，后指线条。

items.en: Lineare meant to draw lines.
items.cn: lineare 意为画线。

items.cn: delineare 意为用线条勾画。

items.en: Delineate entered English for drawing outlines.

items.en: It widened to describing things in words.

intro.en: Delinquency comes from Latin delinquere, de- plus linquere, to leave: a duty left undone.
intro.cn: delinquency 源自拉丁语 delinquere，由 de- 加 linquere（留下）构成：把职责留下不做。

items.en: Linquere meant to leave or let go.
items.cn: linquere 意为离开、放手。

items.en: Delinquere meant to leave a duty undone, to fail.
items.cn: delinquere 意为把职责留下不做，即失职。

items.en: Delinquentia named the failing or the fault.
items.cn: delinquentia 指失职或过失。

items.en: Delinquency entered English for neglect of duty.
items.cn: 十七世纪 delinquency 以玩忽职守义进入英语。

items.en: It came to name minor offences by the young.
items.cn: 十九世纪转而指青少年的轻微犯罪。

items.en: Banks used it for loans that were paid late.
items.cn: 银行用它指逾期还款的贷款。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the linqu- leaving family; the near-meaning group names other failures to act.
note.cn: 形近组共享 linqu-（留下）家族；近义组是其他「没做到」的说法。

sceneCN: 这里 deliver 指「递送」（第 1 个义项：把物品送到某处）；句意是司机在中午前把包裹送到了。

senses.title: Take something to its place
senses.definition: to carry goods, letters or food to the person or place waiting for them
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、信件或食物送到等待的人或地点
senses.example: The driver delivered the parcel before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在中午前把包裹送到了。
senses.why: A thing only counts as sent when it has arrived.
senses.whyCN: 东西只有到了，才算真的寄出去。

senses.title: Give a speech aloud
senses.definition: to speak words to an audience in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式场合向听众讲出一段话
senses.example: She delivered a short speech at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口作了一个简短的讲话。
senses.why: Words too are carried from one mouth to many ears.
senses.whyCN: 话也是被从一个嘴里送到许多只耳朵里的。

senses.title: Do what was promised
senses.definition: to produce the result that was promised or expected
senses.definitionCN: 交出所承诺或所期待的结果
senses.example: The new team delivered results in the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 新团队在第一个月就交出了成果。
senses.why: A promise is only a parcel that has not arrived yet.
senses.whyCN: 承诺不过是一个还没送到的包裹。

intro.en: Deliver comes from Old French delivrer, from Latin de- and liberare, to set free.
intro.cn: deliver 来自古法语 delivrer，底层是拉丁语的 de- 与 liberare（使自由）。

items.en: Liberare meant to set a person free.
items.cn: liberare 意为把人释放、使之自由。

items.en: Delivrer added the sense of handing something over.
items.cn: delivrer 又添上「把东西交出去」的意思。

items.en: English used deliver for freeing and for giving up a thing.
items.cn: 英语用它既表示解救，也表示交出东西。

items.en: The sense of carrying goods to a place grew strong.
items.cn: 把货物送到某地的意思渐渐占了上风。

items.en: One can now deliver a parcel, a speech or a result.
items.cn: 如今可以送包裹、作演讲，也可以交出成果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the liver stem, and the meaning group moves from handing over to sending.
note.cn: 形近组共用 liver 这个词干，近义组则从交给一路走到送出。

entries.definition: the act of being set free
a result that must be handed over
to live through something again in memory
entries.definitionCN: 在记忆里重新经历某事

entries.definition: to give something into another's hands
to cause something to go to a place
to offer something formally to others
entries.definitionCN: 正式地向他人呈交某物

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门口的一声铃开始，落到一个终于变成结果的承诺。

normal.en: A parcel in the van is still only a plan.
normal.cn: 车里的包裹，还只是一个计划。

normal.en: The last step of any journey is a pair of hands.
normal.cn: 任何一段路，最后一步都是一双手。

normal.en: A speech is carried across the room by breath.
normal.cn: 演讲是靠一口气送到屋子对面的。

normal.en: Results are promises that have arrived.
normal.cn: 成果，就是已经送到的承诺。

normal.en: Deliver once meant to set free; now it means to hand over.
normal.cn: deliver 曾表示「使自由」，如今表示「交到手里」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deliver 记成「递礼物」：de 开头，liver 听着像「礼物」，把礼物递到手上，就是送达。

root: 来自古法语 delivrer，底层是拉丁语 liberare（使自由），所以它最早表示「解救、释放」。后来「把东西放出去」变成「把东西交出去」，十五世纪起「送到某地」成为主要意思，又引申出发表演讲与兑现成果。

sensesIntro.en: From a parcel at the door, to words crossing a room, to a promise turned into fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 从门口的包裹，到穿过屋子的话，再到变成事实的承诺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands passing a parcel into other hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手把包裹交到另一双手里。

branches.en: The first sense is a parcel arriving where it was sent.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是包裹到达它被寄去的地方。

branches.en: The second sense carries words instead of goods.
branches.cn: 第二个义项送的是话，不是货。

branches.en: The third sense carries a result that was owed.
branches.cn: 第三个义项送的是欠着的成果。

branches.en: A parcel and a promise both count only when they arrive.
branches.cn: 包裹与承诺，都要到了才算数。

branches.en: Both senses turn something held back into something handed over.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把攥着的东西变成交出去的东西。

intro.en: Deliver has a family of nouns for the act and the person, and an adjective for what never arrived.
intro.cn: deliver 有表示行为与人的名词，也有表示没送到的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is liberare, to free, with de- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 liberare（使自由），前缀 de- 表示离开。

items.meaning: to carry to a place, or to hand over

items.example: The deliverer left the box at the gate.

items.meaning: a result to be handed over

items.example: He delivered a speech on peace.

items.example: The plan must deliver results soon.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划必须尽快交出成果。

definition_en: the act of bringing goods or letters; the way words are spoken; the birth of a baby
core_image: 门口的纸箱上贴着一张写着他名字的条子
scene: 巷口的小店在玻璃上贴了一张纸，说是本城范围内不收运费。The shop offers free delivery within the city.
sceneCN: 这里 delivery 指「投递」（第 1 个义项：把货物送到顾客手中）；句意是这家店在本城范围内免运费送货。

pos.zh: 投递；交付；演讲方式；分娩

senses.title: The bringing of goods
senses.definition: the act of taking goods, letters or food to a customer
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、信件或食物送到顾客手中的行为
senses.example: The shop offers free delivery within the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在本城范围内免运费送货。
senses.why: The last metre of a journey is the one the buyer pays for.
senses.whyCN: 一段路的最后一米，才是买家真正花钱买的那段。

senses.title: The way words are spoken
senses.definition: the manner in which a speech or song is given to listeners
senses.definitionCN: 把讲话或歌曲呈现给听众的方式
senses.example: Her delivery was calm and clear.
senses.exampleCN: 她的表达从容而清楚。
senses.why: The same sentence can be handed over gently or dropped.
senses.whyCN: 同一句话，可以轻轻递过去，也可以扔过去。

senses.title: The birth of a child
senses.definition: the act of a baby coming out of its mother's body
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿从母亲身体里出来的过程
senses.example: The delivery went well and both were healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 分娩顺利，母子都健康。
senses.why: A new life also has to be carried out into the air.
senses.whyCN: 新的生命，也要被送到空气里来。

intro.en: Delivery is deliver plus -y, and deliver goes back to Latin liberare, to set free.
intro.cn: delivery 是 deliver 加 -y，而 deliver 上溯到拉丁语 liberare（使自由）。

items.en: Liberare meant to release a person from a hold.
items.cn: liberare 意为把一个人从束缚中放开。

items.en: Delivrer meant to hand over or to set free.
items.cn: delivrer 意为交出，也意为释放。

items.en: The noun delivery named both rescue and handing over.
items.cn: 名词 delivery 同时指解救与交出。

items.en: Trade gave it the everyday sense of goods arriving.
items.cn: 商业给了它「货物送达」这个日常意思。

items.en: It now also covers the manner of speaking and the birth of a child.
items.cn: 如今它也指说话的方式与婴儿的出生。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the liver shape, and the meaning group names what arrives at a door.
